name: wolframalpha
title: Wolfram Alpha
description: Query Wolfram|Alpha for computational knowledge, short answers, simple image results, and full structured query output for math, science, finance, units, dates, geography, and fact-based problem solving.
useCase: Use for math and science questions, unit conversion, formula evaluation, fact lookup, computational queries, symbolic or numeric results, short factual answers, and structured Wolfram|Alpha output in agent workflows.

documentation.markdown:
Wolfram|Alpha computational knowledge endpoints exposed through PaySponge with
x402 payments.

The live x402 wrapper currently exposes 3 paid `GET` routes: `/v1/result` for
a short textual answer, `/v1/simple` for a static rendered result image, and
`/v2/query` for the full structured Wolfram|Alpha result. These routes are
suited to math, science, finance, date/time, unit conversion, geography, and
other computational knowledge tasks where symbolic or numeric computation is
more reliable than web search or an LLM-only answer.

`/v1/result` and `/v1/simple` cost $0.01 per request and `/v2/query` costs
$0.02 per request. All currently exposed routes accept x402 USDC on Solana
mainnet, Base, and Avalanche.

## Spend-aware usage

- Use `/v1/result` when a short textual answer is enough and reserve `/v2/query`
  for cases that need richer structured output.
- Use `/v1/simple` only when the caller specifically needs an image-style result
  rather than text.
- Use `/v2/query` with `includepodid`, `podtitle`, `podindex`, `scanner`, or
  `podstate` to narrow the returned surface before paying again for broader
  output.
- Reuse `assumption` and `podstate` values returned by earlier `/v2/query`
  results when refining an ambiguous query or driving an Instant Calculators
  workflow, instead of rewriting the query from scratch.
- Prefer one precise computational query over several retries. Tighten the
  input phrasing before paying again.

resource.description: Wolfram|Alpha computational knowledge API — full results, short answers, simple (image), spoken, and conversational endpoints backed by the Wolfram|Alpha computational engine.

ShortInput.name: i
ShortInput.description: The natural-language Wolfram|Alpha query input. The short-answer and simple-image APIs document this parameter name as `i`.
ShortInput.example: How far is Los Angeles from New York?

Units.name: units
Units.description: Select the unit system for measurements and quantities.

Timeout.name: timeout
Timeout.description: Maximum processing time in seconds. Wolfram documents a default of 5 seconds for the short-answer and simple-image APIs.

Background.name: background
Background.description: Background color for the rendered simple-image output. Wolfram documents HTML color names, hexadecimal RGB values, comma-separated RGB values, RGBA-like values with alpha, and `transparent` or `clear`.

Foreground.name: foreground
Foreground.description: Foreground text color for simple-image output.

FontSize.name: fontsize
FontSize.description: Display size of text elements in points. Wolfram documents a default of 14.

Width.name: width
Width.description: Desired width in pixels. Wolfram documents a default of 500 for the Simple API and uses width controls for image-oriented Full Results formats as well.

FullInput.name: input
FullInput.description: The natural-language Wolfram|Alpha query input for the Full Results API.

Output.name: output
Output.description: Switch the documented Full Results response from its default XML shape to JSON. Wolfram documents `output=json`; omitting the parameter returns XML.

Format.name: format
Format.description: Comma-separated list of pod output formats to include. The Full Results docs explicitly describe `image`, `imagemap`, `plaintext`, `mathml`, `minput`, `moutput`, and `cell`.

Assumption.name: assumption
Assumption.description: One or more Wolfram assumption directives. This includes ordinary interpretation assumptions from Full Results and the formula-oriented assumption forms documented by the Instant Calculators API, such as `FSelect_**RAIDArray-`, `*FP.RAIDArray.RAIDLevel-_RAID6`, `*F.RAIDArray.disks-_4`, `*FS-_**RAIDArray.size--`, and `*FVarOpt-_**RAIDArray.spareDisks--`.

PodState.name: podstate
PodState.description: One or more pod-state changes from the `input` attribute of a `<state>` element, used for drilldown and alternate pod views. Wolfram also documents the multiplicity shortcut form such as `2@DecimalApproximation__More digits`.

IncludePodId.name: includepodid
IncludePodId.description: Pod IDs to include in the result. Use repeated parameters for multiple values.

ExcludePodId.name: excludepodid
ExcludePodId.description: Pod IDs to exclude from the result. Use repeated parameters for multiple values.

PodTitle.name: podtitle
PodTitle.description: Pod titles to include in the result. Wolfram documents `*` wildcard matching and repeated parameters for multiple values.

Scanner.name: scanner
Scanner.description: One or more scanner names to include. Wolfram documents both comma-separated and repeated forms.

Location.name: location
Location.description: Location string used to guide geospatial interpretation and local defaults.

LatLong.name: latlong
LatLong.description: Latitude and longitude hint used to determine a location.

Ip.name: ip
Ip.description: Caller IP address to determine location. Wolfram documents this for forwarded end-user requests.

MaxWidth.name: maxwidth
MaxWidth.description: Maximum width to use for returned pod images or cell renderings.

PlotWidth.name: plotwidth
PlotWidth.description: Requested plot width for graphical results.

Magnification.name: mag
Magnification.description: Image magnification factor for certain rendered outputs.

ScanTimeout.name: scantimeout
ScanTimeout.description: Maximum time in seconds for the scan stage. Wolfram documents a default of 3 seconds.

PodTimeout.name: podtimeout
PodTimeout.description: Maximum time in seconds for formatting any one pod before it is dropped from the output.

FormatTimeout.name: formattimeout
FormatTimeout.description: Maximum time in seconds for the entire format stage.
